title: Microsoft–ACTU: shared-intent framework and Workers’ Summit

observations.claim: Microsoft Australia and the ACTU announced a framework on 15 January 2026 that prioritizes worker voice and skilling in AI design, development and deployment.
limits: Bounded to the cited public record and instrument posture.

observations.claim: The framework recognizes union-delegate rights and commits the parties to consult in good faith if disputes arise.
limits: Bounded to the cited public record and instrument posture.

observations.claim: The announcement expressly characterizes the framework as a statement of shared intent.
limits: Bounded to the cited public record and instrument posture.

observations.claim: A Workers’ Summit occurred on 20 April 2026 and included discussion of AI as a management tool and as a tool of work.
limits: Bounded to the cited public record and instrument posture.

observations.claim: The parties reported plans for regular worker-input channels, training and practical pilots.
limits: Bounded to the cited public record and instrument posture.

observations.claim: No named pilot outcome, deployment pause, adverse-decision review, restoration, or audit result is publicly recovered.
limits: Bounded to the cited public record and instrument posture.

findings.claim: The framework is stronger evidence of actual dialogue than a merely aspirational policy because a summit and continuing program are publicly recovered.
limits: No unpublished term, universal prevalence, named-company intent, or complete worker outcome is inferred.

findings.claim: Its explicit shared-intent status prevents promotion to collective bargaining, statutory co-determination, or an enforceable worker veto.
limits: No unpublished term, universal prevalence, named-company intent, or complete worker outcome is inferred.

findings.claim: Good-faith consultation can be a precursor to counterpower, but no public evidence shows authority to suspend or reverse a deployment.
limits: No unpublished term, universal prevalence, named-company intent, or complete worker outcome is inferred.

findings.claim: Named pilot design, worker influence, disputes, remedies and system changes remain open.
limits: No unpublished term, universal prevalence, named-company intent, or complete worker outcome is inferred.
